# Marin Cilic becomes lowest-ranked player in ATP history to win tournament title, in Hangzhou
The former US Open champion entered the 250 tournament ranked 777th, and 0-4 in tour-level matches this season.
* * *
By Ed McGroganPublished September 24, 2024
* * *
WATCH: 373rd-ranked Marin Cilic wins first title since 2021 at Hangzhou Open1:39
You might say the odds were stacked against Marin Cilic at the Hangzhou Open. He entered the 250-level tournament in China with an 0-4 record in tour-level matches this season, ranked 777th in the world rankings, and without an ATP Tour title since 2021. When the soon-to-be 36-year-old dropped the first set of his first match to Zachary Svajda, another quick exit appeared in the offing.
But from then on, Cilic began to resemble the player of his past: a champion. The Croat also entered this tournament with 20 titles to his name, none more significant than the US Open trophy he won 10 years ago. But age, injuries and form conspired to send the veteran plummeting down the tennis totem pole.
“It’s been a difficult period for me, in these last 20 months,” said Cilic. “I’ve lost my ranking, I didn’t play too much.”
> Overcoming all the obstacles 🥹👏[@cilic_marin](https://twitter.com/cilic_marin?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) speaks after winning Hangzhou. [#HangzhouOpen](https://twitter.com/hashtag/HangzhouOpen?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [pic.twitter.com/7bvG2CQnMJ](https://t.co/7bvG2CQnMJ)
> — Tennis Channel (@TennisChannel) [September 24, 2024](https://twitter.com/TennisChannel/status/1838581412515164631?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)
He received a wild card into Hangzhou—and repaid the organizers by going all the way.
While those organizers and the fans would have likely preferred to see Chinese star Zhang Zhizhen prevail, no one could hold back a smile after seeing Cilic once again swing his racquet with success. After dropping that aforementioned set, he dropped just one more in total, capping his stay with a 7-6 (5), 7-6 (5) win.
The smile on his face after match point, and while accepting his championship, said it all.
> World No. 777 ➡️ Hangzhou Champion 🏆  
>

Marin Cilic's Hangzhou 2024 record at World No. 777
Marin Cilic set the ATP Tour record in September 2024 when he won the Hangzhou Open as a wildcard ranked 777th in the world. The Croatian former world No. 3 defeated Zhang Zhizhen in the final, then jumped 565 places to No. 212 in the rankings. It was his 21st career title and first since 2021.

## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
Marin Čilić was born in [Medjugorje](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medjugorje "Medjugorje"), [SR Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SR_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "SR Bosnia and Herzegovina"), a town in [Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzegovina "Herzegovina"), to [Bosnian Croat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croats_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Croats of Bosnia and Herzegovina") parents. He was raised as a [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-12) His father Zdenko Čilić was determined that his sons – Marin and older brothers Vinko and Goran – would have the opportunities he lacked in playing sports. When the first tennis courts in the town were built in 1991, Marin and his friends were among the first to play on them. At the recommendation of [Goran Ivanišević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goran_Ivani%C5%A1evi%C4%87 "Goran Ivanišević"), in 2004, at the age of 15, Čilić moved to [Sanremo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo "Sanremo"), Italy, to work with Ivanišević's former coach, [Bob Brett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Brett "Bob Brett").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-13)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Personal life")]
On 28 April 2018, Čilić married his long-time girlfriend, Kristina Milković in [Cavtat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavtat "Cavtat").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-14) They have two children together, sons Baldo and Vito.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-15)
### Humanitarian work
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Humanitarian work")]
